title: Full-lattice coverage training for the map-cell classifier: every epoch is a complete pass over all 72,712 vantages
hypothesis: Experiment 2's map-cell classification decode was not refuted — it was starved. Its cross-entropy loss started at ln(2970)=8.0 (uniform over cells) and was still falling linearly (8.10 -> 6.22) when training stopped after 83.8 seconds: 8 epochs x 6,000 sampled crops = 48,000 total views for a 2,970-class memorization problem, i.e. ~16 views per cell across all headings, while most of the 72,712-position training lattice was never seen even once. Final mean true-cell probability was e^-6.2 = 0.2%, so max softmax never approached the scorer's 0.3 confidence threshold and the model abstained on every frame — the coverage<0.2 FAIL, not a verdict on the parameterization. The limiting factor is training coverage, not architecture: a model asked to memorize all of Berlin must actually be shown all of Berlin, repeatedly. Measured throughput (48k views in 84s incl. extraction, ~565 views/s on MPS) says a full-lattice pass costs ~2 minutes, so complete coverage was affordable all along — exp 2 used less than 1% of a sensible training budget.
method: Restore experiment 2's CellLocNet (model.py verbatim from runs/20260731_102754_experiment2/model_src/model.py — conv trunk to 160 ch, 2,970-way cell softmax over 128 m cells, within-cell offset head, confidence = winning-cell softmax mass, decode inside the ONNX graph) and change ONLY the training procedure in model/train.py: each epoch is now one full pass over ALL 72,712 lattice positions with a fresh random rotation per position per epoch (streamed in shuffled chunks of 4,096 to bound memory), instead of a 6,000-crop random subsample. With the harness's --epochs 8 this gives 581,696 total views (~196 per cell, 12x exp 2) in a projected ~20 min wall. Cosine LR decay 1e-3 -> 1e-4 across the run (a constant LR is wrong for a 12x-longer schedule). Loss, label smoothing 0.05, batch size 64, architecture, and export all unchanged from exp 2.
expected_outcome: Primary prediction: mission_score drops from the 2.00075 baseline to <= 1.2, target < 1.0. Mechanically: train CE should now approach memorization (well under 2.0 by the last pass; per-pass top-1 train accuracy logged to verify), pushing max softmax above the 0.3 threshold on memorized views, so coverage rises from 0.0 to >= 0.4 and clears the MIN_COVERAGE=0.2 FAIL gate. Because a correctly classified 128 m cell centre is within 90.5 m by construction, correct confident cells convert directly into usable fixes: usable_fix_rate >= 0.35, false_fix_rate <= 0.35. Standing metric check: the improvement must appear in usable_fix_rate itself. Informative failure: if 196 views/cell still leaves coverage near 0 (another 1e9), the bottleneck is not scale but the 160-d GAP descriptor's capacity or rotation invariance — which would redirect the next experiment to capacity/decode, with the per-pass accuracy curve as evidence either way.
eli5: Last time we gave the model a multiple-choice map of Berlin — 3,000 tiles, point to the right one — but we only let it study for 84 seconds, and it never even saw most of the city. It answered every question with a shrug. This experiment changes nothing about the model itself; we just run the full study session: show it every spot in Berlin, eight times over, from different angles each time — about 20 minutes instead of 84 seconds. A student who has actually walked every street can start answering with confidence instead of shrugging.

stages.name: Camera frame
stages.detail: 128×128 px daytime crop, Berlin only, no synthetic lighting variants

stages.name: Feature extractor
stages.detail: small strided conv stack that turns the frame into a compact texture fingerprint (last layer 160 channels)

stages.name: Map-cell classifier
stages.detail: scores all ~3,000 128 m map tiles of Berlin and picks the tile this view belongs to — localization as multiple choice, not coordinate guessing

stages.name: Within-cell offset
stages.detail: small head that nudges the fix from the chosen tile's centre to the exact spot inside it

stages.name: Confidence gate
stages.detail: confidence = the belief mass on the winning tile; belief smeared across tiles means low confidence, so the drone abstains instead of taking a false fix

stages.name: Training signal
stages.detail: cross-entropy on the true tile + offset loss; every epoch now walks the ENTIRE 72,712-position Berlin lattice with fresh rotations (581k total views, ~196 per tile — 12× exp 2's coverage), cosine LR decay for the longer run

implementation_brief:
CONTEXT: experiment 2 (reverted) built CellLocNet; its exact source is preserved at runs/20260731_102754_experiment2/model_src/. The current model/ is the naive baseline regressor. This experiment = exp 2's architecture + a full-coverage training loop.

STEP 1 — model/model.py: replace the current file with runs/20260731_102754_experiment2/model_src/model.py VERBATIM (copy it; do not re-derive). It defines CELL_PX=128, grid_dims(meta), CellLocNet (conv trunk chans [3,32,64,128,160] stride-2 + BN + ReLU, GAP, cls_head Linear(160, n_cells), off_head Linear(160,2) with tanh*0.5, cell-centre buffers baked into the ONNX graph, forward() returns [B,3]=(u,v,conf) with conf = max softmax), build_model(meta), loss_fn(logits, offset_pred, target_cell_idx, target_offset) = cross_entropy(label_smoothing=0.05) + 1.0*smooth_l1, export_onnx, estimate_position. Change NOTHING in it — architecture, loss, label smoothing, and export are pre-registered as unchanged from exp 2.

STEP 2 — model/train.py: start from runs/20260731_102754_experiment2/model_src/train.py (which already imports CELL_PX/build_model(meta)/grid_dims/loss_fn and computes cell/offset targets) and change ONLY the epoch sampling + LR schedule:
(a) Replace sample_epoch's rng.choice subsample with FULL-LATTICE streaming: per epoch, shuffle the complete crops list (rng.permutation over len(crops)), iterate it in chunks of 4096 positions; for each chunk, extract crops with a fresh random angle per position (extract_crop(img, cx, cy, angle)), build the chunk's x as float32/255 plus cell_idx = (cy//CELL_PX)*gw + (cx//CELL_PX) and offset = ((cx%CELL_PX)/CELL_PX-0.5, (cy%CELL_PX)/CELL_PX-0.5) exactly as exp 2 did, then train over that chunk in batches of 64 (one pass, shuffled within chunk), free the chunk, continue. Never materialize more than one 4096-crop chunk (float32 chunk ≈ 800 MB is the ceiling; if you prefer, hold the chunk as uint8 and convert per-batch — either is acceptable). The multi-bucket loop stays (LIGHTING_BUCKETS is a single pass-through entry on this branch, so it iterates once).
(b) --max-crops-per-bucket must still be accepted by the CLI (the harness passes 6000) but no longer controls sampling; log it in train_info as 'max_crops_per_bucket_arg' and note in the docstring that epochs are full-lattice passes.
(c) Add cosine LR decay: torch.optim.lr_scheduler.CosineAnnealingLR(opt, T_max=epochs, eta_min=1e-4), scheduler.step() once per epoch. Adam base lr stays 1e-3.
(d) Per-epoch logging: print epoch, mean loss, top-1 cell accuracy over the epoch's training batches (argmax(logits)==cell_idx, accumulated), and mean max-softmax (accumulate softmax(logits).max(1) means) — these diagnose memorization progress and are required to interpret the result either way.
(e) train_info dict: keep exp 2's fields; set n_train_crops = total views this run (epochs * len(crops)), distinct_vantages_seen = epochs * len(crops), add 'full_lattice_epochs': true, 'final_train_top1': <last epoch's accuracy>, 'chunk_size': 4096. init stays 'from-scratch'.

CONTRACTS TO PRESERVE (frozen scorer depends on these): train.py CLI exactly as-is: --area, --out-dir, --data-dir, --epochs (int), --max-crops-per-bucket (int), --seed; writes <out-dir>/models/<area>.onnx and appends to <out-dir>/train_info.json, prints the info dict as JSON on the last line. ONNX export contract (model/model.py docstring): input 1x3x128x128 float32 in [0,1], output [[u, v, conf]], u/v normalized map coords, conf in [0,1]; opset 17, dynamo=False; whole decode (argmax -> cell-centre lookup -> offset -> conf) INSIDE the graph. Gates: exported ONNX must stay <= 4 MiB (exp 2's identical export was 3,053,335 bytes — do not widen anything) and host latency proxy <= 250 ms (exp 2 measured 1.56 ms).

DO NOT touch: pipeline/ (frozen), autoresearch/, anything in /FROZEN. Budget check: measured throughput ~565 views/s on MPS -> 8 full passes over 72,712 positions ≈ 581,696 views ≈ 17-20 min wall; if extraction proves slower than that, do NOT reduce coverage — it is the experiment.
runtime_budget_note: 8 full-lattice passes ≈ 581,696 views at the measured ~565 views/s ≈ 20 min train wall on local MPS — well inside a sensible round; epochs stay harness-controlled via EPOCHS for dialing.
